html:
A Catholic university in Manila, founded in 1611 by Dominican friars. It holds the oldest university charter in Asia still in use.

It began as a college funded by the will of Miguel de Benavides, the Dominican archbishop of Manila, who left his library and money for a school. It trained priests and, later, lawyers, doctors and officials for the Spanish Philippines. The Pope raised it to university rank in 1645, and in the 18th century it received the title of royal university. Classes were in Latin and Spanish.

Many leaders of the Philippine national movement studied there, among them José Rizal, who later complained of the friars' teaching. Under American rule it remained a Catholic university, and during the Second World War the Japanese used its campus as an internment camp for thousands of Allied civilians. It is one of the largest Catholic universities in the world. See also Doctrina Christiana.
sum: A Catholic university in Manila, founded in 1611 by Dominican friars. It holds the oldest university charter in Asia still in use.
